name: Elioenai
title: Benjamite in the genealogy of Jerusalem
summary: Elioenai is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. He is one of the sons of Shimei and is listed in the genealogies compiled after the return from exile in Babylon. Although he does not play a prominent role in the biblical narrative, his name is preserved as part of the genealogical foundation for the people of Israel after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Listed in the genealogy of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Elioenai is mentioned as one of the sons of Shimei in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, which was recorded after the return from exile.

keyEvents.title: Part of the heads of families of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Elienai belonged to a group of family heads in the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem and were important for rebuilding the community after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Living in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: As part of the lineage of Benjamin, Elienai and his family were counted among those who resided in Jerusalem, the traditional territory of the tribe of Benjamin.

keyEvents.title: The Significance of Genealogies After the Exile
keyEvents.description: The recording of Elienai's lineage was part of the important process of documenting Israel's tribal identity after returning from Babylon.
